terms.ambiguity_notes: prakṛti's Sāṃkhya sense is not a nuance, it is a cosmology: MW's own entry gives 'the original producer of the material world' consisting of the three guṇas -- one of two ultimate principles alongside puruṣa. Rendering 'nature' with prakṛti makes this doctrine assert Sāṃkhya dualism, which the concept does not contain. pramāṇa carries the Nyāya epistemology in which a pramāṇa is a means of VALID knowledge; but this doctrine expressly LICENSES HYPOTHESIS GENERATION and is not a proof, so pramāṇa overshoots in precisely the direction ADAPTATIONIST_COUNTERWEIGHT exists to block. Spanish naturaleza sense 2 ('Principio o fuerza cósmica que se supone rige y ordena todas las cosas creadas') is an attested COSMIC GOVERNING FORCE sitting one sense away from the intended reading, and the concept's own note says it must never be rendered mystically -- the mystical reading is not a translator's invention here, it is available in the dictionary. Latin natura's FIRST L&S sense is 'birth', not 'the natural world'; the natural-world reading is sense II.A. HAZARD DOWNGRADED 2026-07-15 BY ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK, AGAINST THIS FILE'S OWN ARGUMENT: the first pass cited the sense ORDER ('birth' is first) as a hazard while omitting the entry's own frequency labels, which cut the other way. L&S marks sense I 'birth' as '(very rare)' and marks sense II 'Transf.' as '(freq. and class.)'. So the dictionary itself reports that a classical reader meeting natura would OVERWHELMINGLY read the nature/constitution sense, not 'birth'. The ordering hazard as originally stated is therefore largely spurious, and the omission of '(very rare)' is what made it look real -- a true citation deployed to support a claim the unquoted remainder of the same entry undercuts. The residual, and it is much smaller, is that natura's core attested sense II.A is 'the natural constitution, property, or quality OF A THING' -- a thing's nature -- rather than 'the natural world as a whole', so the collective reading the doctrine needs is still not the entry's headline sense. That narrower point survives; the 'birth' point does not. Recorded as a strike rather than an edit, because the defect here is not a wrong quote but a quote used to argue past its own context, which is the harder failure to see and the one SIGNUM SIGNUM MANET exists to catch.
forbidden_mistranslations: प्रकृति (prakṛti) bare -- asserts Sāṃkhya's primordial material principle; a metaphysical claim, not this doctrine.
स्वभाव (svabhāva) -- 'inherent nature, essence'; imports svabhāva-vāda, the doctrine that things act from their own inherent nature, which is a determinism claim the concept does not make.
'naturaleza como principio rector' -- lands squarely on Espasa-Calpe sense 2, the cosmic governing force; the mystical reading the concept forbids.
pramāṇa rendered 'proof' (an attested MW sense) -- the doctrine is explicitly NOT a proof; this single word would convert a hypothesis generator into a warrant.
'natura magistra' / 'nature the teacher' -- a rhetorical topos asserting intent and pedagogy. Nature deleted failures; it did not teach.
